intro_pages.title: Introduction
intro_pages.section1:
Dear friends!

Wherever we are in life, the Holy Spirit invites us into an active friendship with Christ - the Word that became flesh and came to dwell among us (John 1:14). If we want to build a friendship with Christ, we need to learn to listen to Him, to perceive what God wants to tell us. One of the best ways to listen to God is to read His Word regularly.
intro_pages.section2: That is why we want to offer you an ancient way to read God's Word fruitfully and apply it to your life. It is called "Lectio Divina", which literally means "divine reading" but is also translated as "spiritual reading".
intro_pages.section3:
Lectio Divina has been known since the first centuries of the Church. Origen used the Greek phrase thea anagnosis (divine reading) to describe the way to approach God and His will through Scripture.

This practice became common when the desert fathers and mothers made God's Word the basis of their personal prayer. Shortly afterward St. Benedict made Lectio divina the basic rule of Western monasticism. From the earliest centuries to today, Lectio Divina remains a living practice inviting us into an intimate relationship with God.
intro_pages.section4: In 2005 Pope Benedict XVI emphasized that one of the effective ways for the Church to be renewed today is precisely Lectio divina. He said that 'continual reading of Sacred Scripture accompanied by prayer will bring the Church a new spiritual spring.' He clarified this idea by saying: 'Among the many fruits of this new biblical spring I would like to mention the spread of the ancient practice of lectio divina, the spiritual reading of Sacred Scripture. This practice consists in lingering over a biblical text, re-reading it repeatedly, almost chewing it, in order to extract the sap that nourishes meditation and contemplation and becomes life-giving for everyday life. The condition for practicing Lectio divina is that mind and heart are enlightened by the Holy Spirit, the very inspirer of Scripture, and therefore disposed to a posture of reverent listening. This was the typical attitude of the Virgin Mary, symbolically presented in the icons of the Annunciation. It is enough for us to allow the Holy Spirit to lead us - just as Mary did.'
intro_pages.section5: The psalmist confesses: 'Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path' (Ps 119:105). God's Word can also be a light for us so that we see where to walk in this time of confusion and disorientation.
intro_pages.section6:
That is why we want to offer you this journal. Besides the calendar and space for notes, you will find a notebook where you can write down your thoughts. Later these thoughts can help you find answers to life's questions.

In the calendar section you will find the liturgical references to the Gospel of the day. This can help you choose the text for reading and meditation. We also offer you the website www.lectio.one and the mobile app Lectio Divina, which you will find in the App Store or Play Store.

In the mobile app you will find prepared texts that will help you enter this practice. We regularly add Sunday liturgical readings of the Gospel together with meditation, prayer, contemplation, and a simple call to apply God's Word in everyday life. You can also create your own notes that will be ordered by the meditation date. If you use this option, we recommend naming the note after the text you meditate on or a keyword capturing what you reflected on. This makes it easier to return to the Word you meditated on when you look for an answer to a life question.

how.title: How should I proceed?
how.intro: Reading the Bible with the "lectio divina" method – explanation of the steps:

lectio.title: LECTIO – READING
lectio.body: Read a selected text, for example according to the plan for each day. Read slowly, unhurriedly, prayerfully, aloud, and then again at least three times. Let the text act on you; do not try to grasp it only intellectually. Pay attention especially to the words, phrases, or sentences that touched you. In faith we expect God to speak to our soul through the Word and the Spirit.

meditatio.title: MEDITATIO – MEDITATION
meditatio.body:
This second step invites you to reflect on the Word—the words, phrases, and sentences that spoke to you—and let them come to the forefront.
Write them down and allow them to penetrate the depths of your heart. Repeat them again and again, considering the feelings or emotions they stir in you. Ask yourself: 'What is the Holy Spirit telling me through these words?' What do these words mean to me? What is God saying to my heart through them?
This part resembles Mary's response in Luke 2:51 where it says she kept all these words in her heart.

oratio.title: ORATIO – PRAYER
oratio.body:
Prayer according to God's Word (in your own words).
This step encourages a prayerful response. After re-reading and pondering the words, phrases, and sentences that touched you, and after asking the related questions, take these thoughts to heart and craft a prayer—your personal response to the Lord. Tell God what is on your heart; offer Him a prayer of love, gratitude, petition, or intercession. Sit quietly, write the prayer, draw a picture—just respond actively to the word you received.

contemplatio.title: CONTEMPLATIO – CONTEMPLATION
contemplatio.body:
An inner gaze of the heart at Jesus who steps out of the text; a look at Jesus whose characteristic you recognized while meditating on the text. This is the space to rest in God.
We become still and simply remain in God as His beloved. This is not easy and requires patience and discipline.
Stay for a moment in silence and allow the Lord to love you and to plant in your heart the words He has given you throughout this lectio divina process. This is prayer of presence, a movement from conversation to union.

actio.title: ACTIO – ACTION
actio.body: Formulate one short sentence that you will recall throughout the day.

practical.title: Reading the Bible with the "lectio divina" method – practically:
practical.body:
Preparatory step: Choose a short Bible text (a passage from the New Testament). Before you start reading the sacred text, invoke the Holy Spirit. Pray for His presence, become aware that He is with you, ask Him to reveal what is hidden in the text and to guide you. For example: Come, Holy Spirit. Enlighten my mind. Give me love for GOD'S WORD. Help me understand what GOD'S WORD wants to tell me. Help me listen carefully to your instructions.

Second step: Read GOD'S WORD (LECTIO)...
Third step: Meditate (MEDITATIO)...
Fourth step: Pray GOD'S WORD (ORATIO)...
Fifth step: Gaze at God's Word—at Jesus (CONTEMPLATIO)...
Sixth step: Live God's Word (ACTIO)...
Seventh step: Finish your encounter with GOD'S WORD with prayer, especially thanksgiving.

tips.title: What not to forget with this form of reading God's Word:
tips.body: MAKE TIME: Most of us do not have time to spare. This journal together with the app will help you find at least twenty minutes during the day to practice reading God's Word through Lectio divina. Make time! CREATE A SPACE: Truly find a place where you can enter the Lectio process. Jesus is the example—He found time to go to a particular place to spend time in prayer with the Father. PERSEVERE: This is a long-term project. It requires dedication and determination. Perseverance needs to be trained.

how.wish: I wish that time spent with Christ in this way becomes a time when you discover yourself, God's will, and the resolve to persevere in what is good.

about.description:
Lectio Divina is an ancient way of praying with God's word: reading (Lectio), meditation (Meditatio), prayer (Oratio), silence (Contemplatio) and a concrete life step (Actio).

The lectio.one app offers daily biblical readings, a guide through the steps of Lectio Divina, reflections and audio recordings, so you can return to God's word every day and let it guide you.
about.team_description: Meet the people behind the Lectio Divina project who work every day to help you experience a deeper relationship with God.
about.team_m1_bio: Fr. Dušan is a priest of the Žilina Diocese and founder of the Lectio Divina project. His passion is helping people discover a deeper relationship with God through God's word. He serves as executive director of the diocesan pastoral fund KROK, which supports pastoral work and spiritual initiatives in the Žilina Diocese.
about.team_m2_role: Translator and Project Development Team Member
about.team_m2_bio: Adam has been a member of the project since its beginning. He works on English translations while studying law in his second year. He strives to live according to Lectio Divina principles and bring them into everyday life. He is the author of the mypro.one project, which focuses on digital business cards and modern forms of online identity.
about.team_m3_role: Content Coordinator and Heart of the Project
about.team_m3_bio: Kristínka has been part of the project since its beginning and stood by its foundation building. Thanks to her patient work, all data was incorporated into the database, dedicating countless hours to the project. She is the heart of the Lectio Divina team and remains its inseparable part even during maternity leave.
about.team_m4_bio: Sr. Mary Carmen comes from Spain and is a religious sister of the Congregation of Sisters of Our Lady of Consolation. Together with her fellow sisters, she is responsible for translating the Lectio Divina project into Spanish and creates the prayer foundation that accompanies the entire project with spiritual support and prayer.
about.team_m5_role: Graphic and Audio Creator of the Project
about.team_m5_bio: Matúš is the youngest team member – he is only 16 years old and started his practice at the pastoral fund KROK. The idea of the Lectio Divina project captivated him so much that he became its active part. He is responsible for the graphic elements of the project and also takes care of sound generation through ElevenLabs. We are grateful that he is part of the team – he brings creativity, enthusiasm and a fresh perspective.
about.team_m6_role: Creative Author and Visual Architect of the Project
about.team_m6_bio: Benjamín is a filmmaker and university student in Prague specializing in animation and visual effects. In his work, he focuses on original projects that have been awarded at several festivals, and he also shares his experience with children as a lecturer at workshops and film camps. In the Lectio Divina project, he participates in preparing the upcoming Lectio Divina course and helps shape the visual and artistic vision of the entire project.
about.team_m7_bio: Nathanaël is a 7th-year student at an eight-year grammar school and contributes to the Lectio Divina project by translating it into his native language. He is actively engaged in studying foreign languages, first-aid topics, working with young people, and serving in his community. With his enthusiasm and willingness to help, he brings God's Word closer to even more people.
about.team_m8_role: Animated Content Creator and Visual Designer
about.team_m8_bio: Dominik is 18 years old and a classmate of Matúš. In the Lectio Divina project, he focuses on graphic design and creating AI-animated videos, and is also the driving force behind the Potulky Bibliou project. He uses his talent to bring biblical stories to children in an engaging and accessible way. His face and voice will be part of the upcoming animated guide, in which biblical characters and their stories come to life.

potulky.hero_subtitle: We're preparing a family adventure with God's word for children aged 6 to 13. Thanks to your support, 26 stops will come to life, combining videos, games, activities and discovering the Bible together as a family.
potulky.feature1_text: We want to create short animated videos that bring Bible stories to children in an engaging and easy-to-understand way.
potulky.feature2_text: We're preparing a digital booklet in the app that will accompany children throughout the whole journey, offering stories, illustrations and tasks.
potulky.feature3_text: The project will include interactive games and quizzes that help children better understand and remember the Bible stories.
potulky.feature4_text: We want to prepare simple activities that let parents and children experience God's word together at home.
potulky.feature5_text: At the end of the journey we'll prepare a shared contest and prize draw to encourage families to complete the whole adventure.
potulky.feature6_text: Thanks to your support we'll be able to print booklets that reach families and parishes and help children discover the Bible even away from a screen.
potulky.about_title: Help us create a biblical adventure for families
potulky.about_text: We want to create a year-long programme that leads children and parents to God's word in a playful and understandable way. Journey through the Bible builds on the beloved Rorate Advent tradition and offers 26 stops full of stories, videos, games and shared activities. Thanks to your support we can bring this project to families and parishes.
potulky.why_title: We want to help families discover the Bible together
potulky.why_text: Today's children grow up surrounded by screens, yet they often have no way to discover God's word in a way that speaks to their world. We want to create a project that brings families, parishes and children together to discover the Bible. We believe that even a small daily stop can touch a child's heart and bear fruit for a lifetime.
potulky.stops_text: Each stop brings a short video, a page in the booklet and a shared activity that helps families discover the Bible step by step.
potulky.aud1_text: We want to help parents find a simple way to spend time together with God's word.
potulky.aud2_text: We're preparing ready-made materials that parishes, schools and communities can use.
potulky.aud3_text: We want to show children that the Bible isn't just a book of stories, but an adventure they can live every day.
potulky.help_title: Help us lead children to God's word
potulky.help_text: Your contribution helps create the videos, the app, the games, the booklets and materials for families and parishes. Every gift helps bring God's word closer to children and their parents.

kurz.hero_badge: We're preparing a six-part video course
kurz.hero_subtitle: We're preparing a video course that teaches people, step by step, how to pray with God's word. Thanks to your support, six parts on the Lectio Divina method will come to life — from stillness to a concrete act of love.
kurz.about_title: Help us create a course of prayer with God's word
kurz.about_text: Lectio Divina is not just reading the Bible. It is a path of meeting God in his word. We want to prepare a video course that guides the viewer through the six steps of this prayer — from stillness, through reading and meditation, to an act of love. Each part will include teaching, practical guidance and space for personal prayer.
kurz.why_title: So that God's word becomes a place of personal encounter
kurz.why_text: Many people long to read the Bible but don't know how to begin. Others know the text of Scripture but are looking for a way to truly pray with it. We want to create a course that shows, simply and calmly, that God's word is not just a text to study, but a living place of encounter with God.
kurz.path_title: From silence to an act of love
kurz.step1_text: We'll help the viewer enter into silence, quiet the mind and heart, and prepare to listen to God's voice.
kurz.step2_text: We'll show how to read Scripture slowly and attentively, so that God's word can resound personally and deeply.
kurz.step3_text: We'll explain how to let God's word descend into the depths of the heart and ask what God is saying to us today.
kurz.step4_text: We'll lead the viewer to respond to God's word — in thanksgiving, petition, surrender and honest conversation with God.
kurz.step5_text: We'll draw near to the moment of quiet resting in God's presence, where words are no longer needed — only being with the one who loves us.
kurz.step6_text: We'll show how prayer with Scripture can become a concrete act of love in everyday life.
kurz.format_title: We're preparing a course to watch and to share
kurz.fmt1_text: Thanks to your support, professionally filmed and edited parts will come to life, with a calm, contemplative tone.
kurz.fmt2_text: We want to prepare the course in five languages, so it can serve people in Slovakia and abroad.
kurz.fmt3_text: The course will be suitable for personal prayer, but also for communities, parishes, schools and formation meetings.
kurz.help_title: Help us make Lectio Divina available to those who long to pray
kurz.help_text: Your contribution helps create the videos, prepare the content, produce the course and its translations. Every gift helps bring prayer with God's word closer to individuals, families, communities and parishes.

confession.title: Examination of Conscience
confession.subtitle: Preparing for the Sacrament of Reconciliation
confession.setup_intro: Your preparation is protected by the seal of confession: it stays only on this device, encrypted and accessible only with a PIN. Set one now.
confession.unlock_intro: Enter your PIN to access your preparation.
confession.forgot_body: The PIN cannot be recovered — it protects the seal of confession. The only option is to start over: your entire preparation (checks and notes) will be PERMANENTLY deleted.
confession.privacy_note: Seal of confession: your answers and notes never leave this device, are encrypted (AES-256) and excluded from all backups. The app has no microphone access — it cannot listen to anything. We do not track what you check or whether you went to confession.
confession.notes_hint: What I want to confess, what not to forget…
confession.reset_hint: Deletes your entire preparation from this device. PIN remains.
confession.reset_body: Delete your entire preparation (checks and notes)? This cannot be undone.
confession.reset_done: God has embraced you with His love and forgotten everything that weighed you down. Go in peace. 🕊️
confession.info_intro: The examination of conscience is a conversation between you and God. We built it so no third party can enter it — not even us.
confession.info_device_body: Your checked questions and notes are never sent to any server. There is no sync, no cloud, no copy on our side.
confession.info_crypto_body: Data is encrypted (AES-256) and only your PIN or biometrics unlock the key. Without the PIN it cannot be read — which is why even we cannot recover it.
confession.info_backup_body: Your preparation is not part of phone backups or transfers to a new device.
confession.info_mic_body: The app has no microphone access — it cannot listen or record anything. You can verify this in your phone settings.
confession.info_tracking_body: There is no analytics on the confession screens. We do not know what you checked, what you wrote, or whether and when you went to confession.
confession.info_delete_body: The “I went to confession” button permanently deletes your entire preparation. The screen is also protected from screenshots (Android).
confession.info_footer: “I have swept away your offenses like a cloud, your sins like the morning mist; return to me, for I have redeemed you.” (cf. Is 44:22)
confession.disclaimer: Important: This preparation is only an aid for your conscience. The sacrament of reconciliation itself requires a personal encounter with a priest. The app does not replace confession — it helps you prepare for it better and live it in peace.
